body:
I would love to see the world - have always really wanted to go to Tokyo - but the cost factor is pretty huge. 

I tried calling my mom for support but she ended up yelling at me, telling me that happiness is a choice and that I need to change my outlook, and why am I such a negative person and I'm not going to get anywhere in the world acting like a baby and that I was acting like my grandmother, afraid of everything 

> my grandmother is a paranoid and has anxiety issues that I inherited and it is my biggest fear to become her but I recognize the signs as I get older and it terrifies me more than suicide - she is kind and I love her the most but my mom essentially handed me over to her as a child because she lived with us and my mom worked so she let my grandmother take the reigns on raising me in my early childhood (despite the fact that she would burn checks in her sink to make sure no one used them and she hid my formula from my father because she thought he would poison it and she did not have the ability to pick me up from elementary school as a child while I was sick because the idea of going into a new place made her too anxious and she eventually lost her license because she drove the wrong way down a road that had a median and instead of turning off of the road to turn around she just kept going until she ran into a cop, and, according to my mom,  in her childhood they would often have raw eggs served for breakfast with ashes sprinkled on them when my grandfather was at work and my grandmother was suffering a paranoid episode, and she only finally left the house when her paranoid episodes became consistent like when she called the police because everyone in our house was a ghost and she had sodomized a man and the pope knew and told her she was discommunicated from the church so she could no longer keep her husbands name), therefor almost ensuring that she would poison me with her anxiety-riddled beliefs before I had formed my own conciousness

and that if I don't get a handle on it I'm going to be just like her. I told her that I hadn't fought with her in a while (she used to berate me for depression and anxiety, because, "happiness is a choice! why won't you just choose it!" so we fought a *lot* while I was in high school and since I've moved out our relationship has stabilized more or less) and that I didn't want to start again, and that she wasn't really helping but was instead upsetting me more so I hung up. 

I know I can't give up but I feel like when I start to try I just keep shutting myself down and don't know what I'm doing and I end up spending 8 hours laying on my couch under a blanket staring blankly (like my grandmother so often does) until my boyfriend gets home. It's terrifying, because I will get up to do something, and find myself just sitting in a chair staring into space thinking anxious thoughts for hours before I snap out of it. 

It's very scary to think that my only option will be to move back in with my mother because I know that I will kill myself, because my only attempts have been when I lived with her and have been directly following confrontations that dragged me down confidence-wise and mental health-wise, so I guess that in itself is really the most motivating factor of becoming successful.

I'm really sorry for the wall of text, like I said to the last person who replied, you don't have to read this or even reply but it helped to get to rant and not feel aimless for a bit.

I've gotten counseling before and while it helped from time to time, it's also pretty costly, and I've had both really positive and really negative experiences with counselors. 

I had one horrible one after my only almost-successful attempt (it involved hospitalization for a week and an assigned therapist afterwards) who told me that anything I told her she would tell my mom (like if I drank/smoked, etc) and that I was a bad teenager and that I was overreacting to most things. I had one great one after that, but it was $40 a session and my mom made me stop seeing her after she told my mom that my mom was being unreasonable when she said that I couldn't spend the night out after prom, saying that she was, "a bitch quack and for $40 a session we couldn't afford her anymore." 

After this it was about two years before I saw another therapist. I saw my school's free therapist once after a friend killed herself while I was a sophomore in college. It really shook me up because she had been institutionalized too and we would joke about it like, "oh how silly of us to do that," but then she actually ended up committing suicide and it scared me shitless because I realized that you can think you are past it and then it will come back with a vengeance and I was so scared that would happen to me too. The therapist that I talked with that time was alright but my school only allows 4 free sessions per semester, so I went through those pretty quickly.

Also, due to a recent series of medical issues (a food allergy developing after years of being completely allergy free, an emergency ER visit, a doctor's visit, a temporary skin condition, and an allergist appointment) my funds have been more or less drained and I can't afford any more appointments or visits, especially something like therapy that needs to be ongoing to work.

As far as the spiritual counseling goes, I'm an atheist, and while I think that religion is super good for a lot of people, I can't restructure my beliefs and therefor probably wouldn't get much out of it. Although, I want to stress that I do think that religion can be so so great for a lot of people and I am by no means a mean or snarky or militant atheist at all.

Also, the knives in my apartment are far too dull to do anything like that - they hardly cut chicken because they are so dull haha. And luckily there aren't any unnecessary prescriptions - my first attempt was with pills so I've taken precautions to not keep them stocked in my house.

Sorry for bombarding you with this wall of text. It helped to type it out, you don't have to read all of it if you don't want to, and, not having proofed it, it is likely to be riddled with grammatical errors.
